q1cb683131a.t: The mechanism of inspiration, resulting from the descent of the diaphragm, causes intraabdominal pressure to increase as intrathoracic pressure decreases.

q25650249d5.src: Patton 9e · Ch 30 Circulation of Blood · p. 708
q25650249d5.quote: vasomotor center of the medulla sends sympathetic signals to certain blood vessels
q25650249d5.t: During exercise, the vasomotor center of the medulla sends sympathetic signals to certain blood vessels to change diameter and thus shunt blood away from “maintenance” organs, such as the digestive organs in the abdomen, and toward the skeletal muscles.

q95f949735b.quote: If blood consisted only of plasma, the maximum oxygen that could be transported would be only about 0.3 ml
q95f949735b.t: If blood consisted only of plasma, the maximum oxygen that could be transported would be only about 0.3 ml of O2 per 100 ml of blood.

qc7e3923d97.src: Patton 9e · Ch 30 Circulation of Blood · p. 714
qc7e3923d97.quote: useful in reducing abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension).
qc7e3923d97.t: Because angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) regulates the amount of available angiotensin II, drugs that act as ACE inhibitors can reduce angiotensin II and thus block vasoconstriction—an effect that is useful in reducing abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension).

qcba59a0c25.quote: external respiration (ventilation and pulmonary gas exchange), transport of gases by blood, and internal respiration
qcba59a0c25.t: This chapter and the next are organized around the principle that respiratory function includes external respiration (ventilation and pulmonary gas exchange), transport of gases by blood, and internal respiration (systemic tissue gas exchange and cellular respiration).

qee1ee274dc.quote: cardiac control center and the vasomotor center in the medulla.
qee1ee274dc.t: Carotid sinus and aortic baroreceptors detect changes in blood pressure and feed the information back to the cardiac control center and the vasomotor center in the medulla.

qef65834634.quote: foramen ovale normally becomes functionally closed soon after a newborn takes the first breath
qef65834634.t: The foramen ovale normally becomes functionally closed soon after a newborn takes the first breath and full circulation through the lungs becomes established.
